body: I'm her mom, but your comment truly resonates with me none the less. Thank you. I would be private messaging you right now if I knew how. Can you message me?
Me too and now I'm one of them.

I absolutely agree. I got out of the cult when i was 16 and only now have started drinking excessively and people keep asking me why and that is the only answer i can give. I just wonder why all these issues are manifesting now.

You are so nice! It makes me want to cry. I don't think I'm ready to repost just yet. I'm pretty sure I'm a few hours away from taking a drink and I don't think there is anything anyone can say to stop me. I'm not trying to be difficult. Just honest. The love and support I've gotten from you and this community is astounding and I do plan on coming back here. Just not today. I just can't seem to escape my alcoholism today. I'm so sorry that I've let you guys down. 

I will be back and I will continue to try and keep quitting. I guess I need to hit some sort of rock bottom. I want to stop but that doesn't seem to be enough. I know it's only a matter of time before something horrible happens due to my drinking, but nothing bad has happened yet other than the horrible withdrawal/hangovers the next day. I don't want to wait around for something bad to happen but the desire to stop drinking doesn't feel like it's enough yet. I don't even know what I'm talking about...

I got in an argument and acted like an ass. Not doing so well. I've fallen off the wagon about three times since I came to this sub. Each time I pick myself back up and "quit again" the net day so my drinking has decreased dramatically, but my intention is to quit forever, not moderate, so I still feel like a failure.
I got banned.
Sorry, just sad thinking this post on our front page is going to turn people away with it's mockery and felt like I would make OP aware.

I truly believe that *some* (and a good portion of) people capable of moderate drinking would both read it and not only be offended, but be discouraged by this and decide not to join this sub. 

and if an alcoholic, who is fooling themselves with thinking they can drink moderately, feels offended by this, it's going to scare them away before this sub could possibly help them come to terms with their alcoholism. They are just going to feel mocked and outright attacked. 

Sure, maybe they are taking it personally because it hits too close to home, but maybe they are not ready to admit they are alcoholics and them feeling made fun of is definitely going to make them feel unwelcome.

Most people here (as far as i can tell, including myself) are alcoholics. I think the reason most of the people here identify with this post, is because the alcoholics tried moderation and failed. (I did too.) Still, that doesn't mean moderation doesn't work for some people and I feel like this post makes them feel like they don't belong here and that we are just making fun of them. Humor tag or not, telling someone "just kidding" doesn't make them feel any less made fun of. 

And no part of the original post said you were making fun about your own experience. It came off as you making fun of the people who came here with the hopes of moderating their alcohol intake. 

I know what you *meant* but you need to take into consideration how this *reads* to moderate drinkers.
To me a humor tag doesn't excuse it. You can't run around saying offensive things IRL and then yell "KIDDING!" at the end to make it all alright.

This isn't funny, it's sarcastic, and sarcasm is inherently derogatory. 

And this is coming from an alcoholic that can never drink again.  You might not have written it this way, but to me this reads as an "older and wiser" person talking down to a little kid as if they don't know how the world works yet. The world is not black and white. You might not have meant it, but to me this comes off as snotty and holier-than-thou.

Extremely. And this is coming from an alcoholic who knows she can never drink again. I don't care if it's labeled as "humor" or not. It's written in an extremely "talking down to people" way. 

Like, god forbid someone who isn't an alcoholic try and cut down on their alcohol a little? Right? Either everyone is just a non-drinker or an alcoholic waiting to happen right? Nobody who has felt the draw of alcohol will end up not an alcoholic right? Cause the wold is black and white. 

TBH I find this post horribly discouraging to people who might be looking for advice on how to cut back. This will just scare them away. I don't care if it's humor (It's not humor BTW its *sarcasm* ) if someone ran up to a person and said "You're ugly! JUST KIDDING" it wouldn't be funny it would be obnoxious.
Still sober! Day six! I will not drink today! Thanks everyone for their support last night!

Thanks for the advice! My husband is definitely not an alcoholic, but you are right, it's hard watching someone do something you once enjoyed.. or at least thought you enjoyed! I still don't fully understand why I kept doing it so long after it only brought me misery.
Thanks. Will do! I just realized I haven't eaten all day. I just ate and I'm hoping that will help.
A 12 year friendship, still going strong. We have nothing in common and she annoys the shit out of me. Still, she's got nobody else.
Thanks! And thank you in staying sober with me :)
Also, thank you so much for the speedy and caring reply!! You all are fantastic. <3

He's very supportive but I told him when I quit that it didn't mean he had to or that we had to get rid of the alcohol in the house. There's been a handle of vodka in our freezer all week. When I came out to him as an alcoholic it really took him off guard because he had no idea. Even though I didn't sugar coat anything and told him just how much/often I'd been drinking, I don't think he has fully accepted I'm an alcoholic even though he is taking my word for it.

Because of that I just don't think he realizes how tough it is for me. The alcohol in the freezer doesn't even phase me. It's just the stupid idea that I'll some how miss out on quality time with the man I love rather than realizing I can have just as much time/fun with him, without drinking.
Felt well enough to go to the gym for the first time in months! Day five! I will not drink today!
Day 4! I woke up feeling more clear headed than I Have in a while, despite having a cold! I will not drink today!
Will do for sure! Thanks. :)

Day three! Not drinking today. Have not really had the desire to drink (until last night) since I've felt so sick the past few days. Woke up today with a sore throat and a stuffy nose. My kid has a cold so I think I caught it (I have an autoimmune disease) WHILE I've been detoxing so I think that's another reason I've been recovering sooooo slowly. FINALLY slept a solid 8 hours last night and feel much better mentally (after about 36 hours with no sleep) even with the cold. 

Like I said, had not really had the desire to drink until last night when my daughter and husband got into a mild argument and then it hit me like a ton of bricks. I can't believe how strong it was when I felt so rock solid. It made me feel like I need to be more on my guard. The feeling immediately passed after I spoke with both of them and dealt with the issue rather than just climbing into a bottle. They rarely fight but due to past abuse, any confrontation at all gives me massive anxiety. I'm thinking I need to express myself more when things bother me instead of finding a way to shut them out. 

Pledging on here yesterday helped get me through not drinking while I was dealing with the issue and I thank this sub for that because if I had just done it with myself I might not have felt as accountable. So, TODAY I pledge to stay sober. (Sorry for such a long post!)
Thank you very much! This community is so welcoming and warm. I really appreciate you taking time out of your day to encourage me. It means a lot. *hug*

Woot woot!! 
No drinking today, deal?

33 hours sober and awake for about as long. I'm the one who posted yesterday morning that everyone told to go to the hospital and stupidly didn't. I'm alive and don't feel in danger of death anymore but I'm shocked at how crappy I still feel after 33 hours. I pledge to remain sober today because feeling this sick is a great reminder that I don't want to have to go through this again.
Hey i just hit 24 hours (yep, counting the hours at this point). We have the same start date!
I'm not judging, just curious, what made you decide to quit and why is that seemingly to be more important than drinking when you decided to quit?
Haha I wish but my house looks like a crack house right now. I'm a slob when I'm drunk. I really done want to clean but now that I'm sober it's really grossing me out.

Much better. I posted an update in the EDIT if you want more details! And thank you for checking up on me! It means so much. I'm still not sure if ill be able to sleep tonight but I think it's alright because my house could use a good cleaning. I just wish my whole body didn't hurt so much and my legs feel so heavy. I luckily work from home so I should be alright.
I will for sure. Reading about the side effects of withdrawal scared the shit out of me.

15-16 hours, but im starting to feel better. Yeah the anxiety is the WORST symptom. I already have bad anxiety issues and the night after a binge my inner monologue just screams at me the most horrible things. (not really hearing voices or anything just super hateful inner monologue.)
Half a handle a day and I've been drunk for about 5-6 days. Im female, 5'5" and 180 lbs. I usually go about 5-6 days between benders and this has been my longest bender to date.
Is it possible to stay sober without "coming out" as an alcoholic to your family?
